stories.delivered_paragraph: Trump Media & Technology Group has launched Truth API, a paid real-time feed promising Wall Street firms and institutional investors the fastest access to influential Truth Social posts. The service raises ethical and legal questions because President Donald Trump’s account, with about 13 million followers, can move markets and his family remains the company’s majority shareholder. The arrangement could let investors pay for an edge on presidential statements while a family-linked company profits from them.

stories.delivered_paragraph: India has introduced legislation that could allow merchants to be charged for some transactions on its Unified Payments Interface, challenging the zero-fee model in place since 2020. UPI processed a record 23.66 billion payments worth ₹29.88 trillion, or about $313.4 billion, in July, while banks and fintechs argue state support is no longer sufficient to sustain the network. Any new merchant fee would test how India funds a payments system that has become central to daily commerce.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Apple is developing an iPhone-to-Windows copy-and-paste feature for European Union users after Microsoft asked it to open Universal Clipboard beyond Apple devices. The change would let people move content between an iPhone and a Windows PC, a capability already available across Apple’s Mac, iPad and Vision Pro ecosystem. It is another practical consequence of the EU Digital Markets Act, which is forcing Apple to make connected-device features work with third-party products.

stories.delivered_paragraph: A multistate lawsuit challenging Paramount’s proposed $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery has focused scrutiny on who would control CNN and CBS, particularly Larry Ellison’s influence through the acquiring company. Paramount chief executive David Ellison has disputed the suit’s framing, while Ari Emanuel has said he has a plan to address fears about editorial control. The dispute turns a media-industry consolidation fight into a test of whether ownership changes could compromise the independence of two major news networks.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Crowds in Gaza City held a mass funeral for 112 Palestinians, mostly women and children, whose bodies were recently recovered from rubble left by an Israeli strike on a residential block in November 2023. The two-week recovery operation found members of the Abu Sharia and Hassayna families, including 40 children and 38 women. The burial, described as Gaza’s largest of its kind, highlights how casualties from the war’s early bombardments are still being uncovered.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Cameroon’s President Paul Biya, 93 and absent from public view for nearly two months, has reshuffled the military and promoted five colonels to brigadier general. He also reappointed Raymond Jean Charles Beko’o Abondo to command the elite presidential guard, a role he has held since 2013. Though such changes are common under Biya, the timing has intensified concern about his health and the stability of his long-running government.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Ukrainian overnight strikes hit two Wildberries warehouses in Russia’s St Petersburg and Tver regions, while an industrial site near Moscow was struck, killing at least five people and injuring 10. The attacks extend Ukraine’s campaign against logistics infrastructure far from the front as both sides continue long-range strikes.

stories.delivered_paragraph: A July Institute for Supply Management survey showed US manufacturing expanding at 55.6, its fastest pace since May 2022, with production rising 6.3 points and employment growing for the first time in 33 months. But the prices index remained high at 71.1, marking a 22nd straight month in which more manufacturers reported higher costs than lower ones. The combination of stronger activity and persistent price pressure complicates the Federal Reserve’s inflation outlook.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Options trading in SpaceX has drawn unusual attention to a $330 call contract expiring Friday, with more than 450,000 open positions—at least seven times the next most popular contract. The trade would require a sharp rally to pay off, and CNBC’s options-flow analysis suggests a large institution may be using the inexpensive calls as a hedge rather than a straightforward bullish bet. The position underscores intense speculation around the recently public company and the risks of reading options activity at face value.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Palantir shares jumped 27% after the software company reported second-quarter revenue up 93% from a year earlier to $1.94 billion, beating the $1.8 billion expected by analysts. Commercial revenue rose 149% to $764 million as customers sought AI tools that let them retain control of their data, while government revenue increased 90%. The results strengthen Palantir’s case that demand for so-called sovereign AI is translating into unusually rapid growth at scale.

stories.delivered_paragraph: A MarketWatch analysis flags a lesser-discussed issue in retirement planning alongside Social Security’s broader funding gap: delaying benefits can raise not only monthly payments but also the cost-of-living adjustments attached to them. Claiming at age 70 therefore produces a permanently larger inflation-linked benefit than claiming earlier. The point matters for households weighing when to file, because the decision affects long-term income and the program’s eventual benefit obligations.
